report.headline: Final POE50 for NSW1 interval ending 2026-07-31 07:30 AEST (UTC+1000) = 11082.0 MW; actual = 11178.0 MW (error −96.0 MW).
summary: AEMO's final operational-demand POE50 for NSW1 for the half-hour ending 2026-07-31 07:30 AEST (UTC+1000) was 11082.0 MW [ev0550].
The same run's POE10 was 11255.0 MW [ev0554] and POE90 was 10909.0 MW [ev0555].
Measured operational demand for that half-hour was 11178.0 MW [ev0551].
The forecast error (POE50 − actual) for that interval was −96.0 MW [ev0552], i.e. −0.86 percent [ev0553].
The compare_forecast_actual result classed the actual as "within POE90-POE10" for this interval (same run/pair).

numeric_claims.text: Mean absolute error (MAE) for the paired range = 397.62 MW

possible_explanations.statement: Short-term demand variability around 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z might not have been captured by the final run's inputs, so the actual fell between the published POE90 and POE10 despite the small POE50 error.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Examine the half-hour and available five-minute or adjacent half-hour measured demand series for 2026-07-30T21:00:00Z and 2026-07-30T21:30:00Z (evidence examples: ev0524, ev0525) to see if within-interval variability explains the difference between POE50 and the actual.

possible_explanations.statement: A small, run-to-run forecast bias (systematic underforecast by a few hundred MW across nearby intervals) could be present and might explain why many later targets show negative errors.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare errors (POE50 − actual) across the paired targets in the same run to check for a consistent sign or magnitude (MAE ev0628 and per-interval errors such as ev0552).
